example_docs: The Intel NUC is a great little computer with the exception of the internal antenna.  It works alright for the low frequency wifi band but for the 5G the NUC is not a good receiver if your computer is in a different room than the wifi.  There is a solution that involves drilling holes in the case and getting external connectors, but this device easily plugs into the USB3 in the back and works without downloads on Windows 10 (Pro).  You end up with 2 wifis, and Windows 10 separates them into a wifi and wifi2.  Actually, my NUC PC was able to detect the 5G with the original built in card (wifi) once this device was plugged in to the USB3, without switching to wifi2.  That raises the question, could an antenna with no electronics at all could somehow work?  Anyway, this works well so far, but time will tell.

example_docs: Love this portable laptop stand. Very sturdy and my laptop isn't heating up as it did before cos there is space for the air to flow.

TL:DR - It does what it is supposed to do with no muss, no fuss.

Details?
Well, some assembly is required but I got through it without a blood sacrifice to the assembly gods. That's a rarity.
All required parts and tools for assembly are included, with each set of parts in a separate marked pouch in a bandoleer. Very nice.
The same for the TV mounting parts. You will need a Philips head screwdriver and a tape measure for that stage, though. Make sure they're handy.
Instructions are well written and organized, and properly illustrated so you can align the pieces correctly on the first try.
Take it nice and steady and it'll come together easily.

Tips?
1- You'll need your third hand early, to mount the vertical riser to the base (which is piano black, pretty but a fingerprint magnet). Alternately, get a box or two of the right height to support the riser and work horizontally. Much quicker and easier.
2- The crossbar the TV attaches to is two pieces tightly held together by two screws each. The metal is thick and obviously heavy and it can probably do more than the recommended weight. But I wouldn't try it. If it says 88 pounds, believe them. Don't push it.
3- When it come time to mount the TV get an assistant. You do not want an accident that late in the game.

Happy viewing.

example_docs: [[VIDEOID:6c014bd4a33712078a237b14d7c4ae80]] This is another fringe curtain I ordered as a backdrop for my YT videos. I like that this is matte silver and not too shiny because all the extra lightning needed for video can add extra flash and that’s not what I wanted. It is really easy to install. First you should carefully unwrap it, remove the protective film on the top and stick the upper part to desired surface. I initially didn’t place it in straight line because I couldn’t reach far enough but I was able to remove it from the wall and place it again. My wall is matte paint (non-glossy paint), slightly grainy textured (not a popcorn wall) and it holds well. It will stick to number of surfaces like wood, plastic, metal, wallpaper and practically whichever flat surface. The fringes are about 1/4in allowing for rich effect, much better than 1/3 or 1/2 of an inch. Overall I’m pleased with this purchase and love the ease of adding more character to my videos by simply using different fringe curtains as a backdrop. It’s reasonably durable and will last as long as you don’t yank on it.

Our old desktop finally failed (wouldn't even turn on) and it was the only connection we had to our parallel port Brother 8840D printer. The parallel-to-USB converter at Office Depot and most similar stores was around $40--and the guy I talked to at OD told me that it probably wouldn't work for what I wanted and that I should call Brother to make sure before I purchased it (which seemed odd, since that was what it was for). I found this one Amazon for $13. I have a Mac, so I was doubly worried (the packaging does not say it's Mac-compatible), but the reviews here from other Mac users who said it did work for their printers made me think it was worth a try.

I got it, I opened it, I used it to connect the Brother printer to my Mac Pro. It worked. Immediately. The printer showed up in the queue and worked with all its functions. I was astonished--I usually don't get technology to work without several hours of investigation and experimentation.

Anyway, if you have an old parallel-port printer and a new USB-only computer and need to connect them up, this is definitely worth a try, whether you've got a PC or Mac. Worked for me.
